A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMPFN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary materials are readable and support matching content across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMPFN benchmark accuracies, projector ablations, low-data experiments and supplementary encoder and regularization analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original MMPFN experiments and adds attention measurements, token-repetition controls, FiLM comparisons and encoder results.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, MGM and CAP operations, frozen modality encoders, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. FiLM and alternative encoders are evaluated as comparison variants; they do not replace components of the proposed default method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain PU20, CBIS-DDSM Mass/Calc, Airbnb, Salary, Cloth and PetFinder, with the same prediction tasks and modality families. New analyses reuse this coverage. Figure 2 drops Cloth curves, but the ELECTRA-only classification setup remains described; sample-count revisions concern E3.

E2.justification: v3 adds TabSTAR to the four tabular-text comparisons in Table 3 and evaluates FiLM against CAP in new Table 6. FiLM was previously only discussed as related work. The existing main benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises Airbnb's reported train/test counts from 5,465/1,367 to 18,316/4,579 and Calc's training count from 1,546 to 1,545. New protocols include 32 versus four repeated sets of 32 versus 128 tokens, and attention measurements averaged over 12 layers. The substantial sample-count revision is documented without explaining whether it corrects reporting or reflects rerun experiments.

E4.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the mechanism analyses: Figures 3 and S2 measure attention allocation across five datasets, and Table 4 separates token count from representation quality using repeated tokens. It also adds CAP-versus-FiLM ablations, ResNet50 comparisons and ELECTRA-versus-DeBERTa results. Figure 2 removes the previous Cloth sensitivity curves.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds {0,1,2,3,4}, report averaged accuracies, and retain Figure S1's mean-and-variance reporting across five seeds. No additional repeated-run count, confidence interval, significance test or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Shared headline accuracies are retained, but substantial new results cover attention allocation, token repetition, FiLM and encoder alternatives. Added TabSTAR scores change MMPFN's PetFinder text rank from first to second: 39.04 versus TabSTAR's 41.53, with average rank changing from 1.75 to 2.25. Table 6 newly reports FiLM's 55.48 average versus CAP's 57.37. Cloth's Figure 2 results are removed.

T1.justification: The appendix adds asymptotic parameter-count expressions for projector variants, including O(N(d²+d/2)) for MGM, supporting a capacity argument. The attention definitions and approximation in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged, and no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: extending TabPFN to multimodal inputs, addressing overcompression and attention imbalance with MGM/CAP, competitive performance, modality scaling and low-data robustness. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations distinguishing token-count effects from representation quality, attributes FiLM's limitations to shared channel-wise modulation, and argues that projector gains are not solely due to capacity. It also interprets the text-encoder comparison as evidence of relative stability across encoder choices. Existing low-data and alignment interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds projector parameter-budget estimates and technical descriptions of the new comparisons, including FiLM conditioning and attention aggregation. Existing optimizer settings, training budgets, preprocessing instructions and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: TabSTAR is newly cited and compared, while FiLM gains an explicit role as an alternative to CAP. The broader research positioning remains stable. Most other bibliography edits update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate references rather than introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: Several related-work, method and results paragraphs are condensed, headings and captions are edited, and CAS is corrected to CAP. v3 adds acknowledgements and removes the separate supplementary experimental-setup heading while retaining its content. The main narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer labels and a legend, and Figure 2 is redesigned to show only PU20. v3 introduces attention plots in Figures 3/S2 and Tables 4, 6 and S3, expands existing comparison tables, and relocates retained heatmaps, ablation tables and learning curves. These materially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 largely supported attention imbalance through accuracy curves and an approximation; v3 adds direct attention measurements and repeated-token controls, strengthening that central explanation. TabSTAR and FiLM broaden the comparisons. These gains support a modest overall improvement, tempered by the removed Cloth curves and the unexplained Airbnb sample-count revision despite unchanged shared accuracies.
